results.name: ClearFake WebDAV infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
results.description: An investigation revealed a sophisticated cryptocurrency and credential-stealing operation using Amatera stealer as the primary payload. The attack chain leverages Cloudflare Workers to inject JavaScript stored on BNB Smart Chain, presenting fake Google CAPTCHA prompts that lead to WebDAV-based DLL execution. Two parallel infection chains were identified, one loading through a DLL named 'pf.ch' and another through 'verification.google', both delivering Amatera stealer with different secondary payloads. The 'pf.ch' variant deployed ZigCryptoStealer via NativeAOT loader and a Go-based reverse proxy, while the 'verification.google' variant installed NetSupport Manager with C2 infrastructure in Russia. The operation affects numerous countries with primary focus on stealing cryptocurrency wallets, credentials from password managers, and various authentication data through extensive collection rules targeting over 400 applications.

results.name: Phishing Campaign Abuses Microsoft Power BI to Deploy Rogue RMMs
results.description: In September, a phishing campaign exploited legitimate Microsoft Power BI domains to distribute rogue ScreenConnect remote monitoring tools. Attackers sent phishing emails with embedded links redirecting victims to fake reference documents hosted on Power BI infrastructure. Clicking 'Download Reference' opened attacker-controlled websites that fingerprinted victims' systems and browsers before triggering malicious ScreenConnect installer downloads. The attack deployed multiple ScreenConnect instances for persistent remote access, with the second client connected to attacker infrastructure. Following deployment, threat actors executed defense evasion tools and created scheduled tasks running persistence scripts every two minutes. The campaign used browser fingerprinting and Telegram bots to filter victims and track infections, while abusing trusted Microsoft domains to bypass email security controls and increase attack credibility.

results.name: FortiBleed Operations Continue Targeting Exposed Systems Leading to Reports of Lockouts
results.description: FortiBleed is an active global credential-compromise campaign targeting internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with over 86,644 compromised devices verified across 194 countries. The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, enabling threat actors to harvest and crack authentication data at scale using distributed GPU clusters. Attackers scan for exposed FortiGate SSL VPN portals, collect credentials through stuffing and password spraying, and crack stolen password hashes offline. Once access is gained, they create new administrative accounts for persistence and conduct Active Directory enumeration to expand access. Affected organizations may experience lockouts as threat actors delete or modify existing accounts. The operation functions as an initial-access broker, with connections observed to INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates, representing a significant threat requiring immediate defensive action.

results.name: 16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Steal Cryptocurrency Wallet Credentials
results.description: A coordinated campaign of 16 malicious Firefox extensions has been identified targeting cryptocurrency wallet users. The extensions masquerade as wallet portals, desktop utilities, and browser tools while intercepting recovery phrases and private keys during wallet import flows. Four large extensions clone Rabby Wallet (misspelled as Raabby WaIIet), while twelve smaller extensions impersonate OKX Wallet. All variants capture 12- or 24-word mnemonics and private keys, transmitting stolen credentials to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers endpoints. Fifteen extensions communicate with icy-star-f45c.workers.dev infrastructure. The campaign reuses code markers, network infrastructure, and credential-handling logic, indicating connection to crypto-theft operations identified in August 2026. Mozilla has unpublished these extensions. Users who entered credentials should immediately create new wallets and transfer assets.

results.name: DarkSword/Coruna Open Directory Finding
results.description: Five hosts exposed the complete DarkSword/Coruna iOS exploitation platform through open directories, revealing an active commercial exploitation-as-a-service operation. The platform targets cryptocurrency wallets across 18 different applications, extracting BIP39 recovery phrases and conducting automated theft. Analysis of the production server recovered 11 victim recovery phrases, 179 device loot directories, and a 75-account control-plane roster indicating an agent/reseller model. A separate China-based operator is deploying identical tooling through independent infrastructure at 66ds[.]lol, representing a distinct threat actor from previously documented DarkSword users. The infrastructure was operationally active during analysis, with beacon telemetry showing Chinese iOS devices polling every three seconds for hours. Development work targeting iOS 26 via CVE-2026-31001 was discovered but remains undeployed.

results.name: Inside PhantomPolia: Remus Stealer Delivery via Donut Shellcode in ClickFix Campaign
results.description: LevelBlue observed a ClickFix campaign delivering Remus Stealer through compromised websites using PhantomPolia, a JavaScript loader that retrieves encrypted configurations from Ethereum Sepolia smart contracts via public RPC endpoints. The loader decrypts configurations locally using PBKDF2 and AES-GCM to obtain C2 domains. Victims are tricked into executing PowerShell commands that retrieve and decrypt additional configurations using AES-CBC before downloading bundled installers containing AutoIt executables. The AutoIt script decrypts embedded Donut-packed shellcode and executes it from allocated memory, ultimately loading Remus Stealer. This information-stealing malware collects system data, credentials, browser information, password managers, and cryptocurrency wallets. Stolen data is compressed using custom methods and encrypted with ChaCha20 before exfiltration to attacker-controlled servers.

results.name: TensorLake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Attack
results.description: The Tensorlake npm SDK version 0.5.144 was compromised in a ChainDrop/Shai-Hulud supply chain attack, affecting a package with approximately 12,000 weekly downloads. The malicious release contains obfuscated code that harvests credentials from multiple sources including npm tokens, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes configurations, SSH keys, and AI development tools. A preinstall hook executes the payload during installation, establishing persistence through scheduled tasks and supporting remote code execution. The attack uses an Ethereum contract to resolve command-and-control endpoints and implements a dead-man switch that monitors stolen GitHub tokens, triggering destructive actions if revoked. The malicious code can self-propagate by republishing compromised versions to other packages associated with the victim's publishing identity, extending the worm's reach across the npm ecosystem.

results.name: RMM Tools Being Distributed Through Phishing Attacks (ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, N-able)
results.description: Multiple Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools are being distributed through phishing campaigns involving video files and email attachments. Threat actors exploit legitimate RMM solutions like ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, and N-able to gain remote access to compromised systems while evading security detection. These tools, typically used for legitimate IT administration purposes, are weaponized through various delivery methods including LNK files, BAT scripts, VBS files, and PDF documents disguised as business documents. The campaigns leverage social engineering tactics, presenting fake Adobe Acrobat updates, DocuSign viewers, and document access prompts to trick victims into installing these remote access tools. Each RMM tool contains configuration data linking back to attacker infrastructure, including deployment IDs, account identifiers, and command-and-control server addresses embedded within installation files.

results.name: StyleSmuggler: Magento and Adobe Commerce 0-day RCE under active attack
results.description: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability dubbed StyleSmuggler affects all current versions of Magento and Adobe Commerce, including 2.4.9, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Active exploitation began on September 4th, 2026. The attack operates in two stages: injecting malicious PHP code into Magento's template system using styles properties to evade safeguards, then executing the poisoned code via failed payment emails. Upon successful compromise, attackers deploy a Rust-based backdoor disguised as legitimate system processes (kworker, fc-cache, or chronyd) that connects to command and control servers. The backdoor uses NTP-shaped UDP traffic for C2 communication to evade detection. A second unrelated attacker has also been observed exploiting the same vulnerability to deploy PHP web shells. Affected merchants should deploy immediate mitigation measures, scan for compromise, and temporarily disable GraphQL until an official patch is released.

results.name: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign
results.description: In June 2026, researchers uncovered BigBear 2.0, a rebranded Evilginx2-based phishing-as-a-service framework targeting Microsoft 365 credentials globally. The operation, managed by operator 'General Boss', deployed 42 VPS nodes primarily hosted on Vultr infrastructure, utilizing the 'offy' phishlet configuration. The platform employed adversary-in-the-middle techniques with geo-matched residential proxy pools across 69 countries, real-time Telegram exfiltration, and automated cookie replay to bypass MFA. The campaign exfiltrated 5,137 credential records including 474 complete MFA-bypassed authentications, 1,032 plaintext passwords, and 4,148 session cookies, affecting 3,331 unique victim IPs across 40+ countries. The multi-user PhaaS panel was leased to at least five identified affiliate operators. Custom JavaScript injections disabled FIDO2/WebAuthn MFA while residential proxies bypassed anti-bot detection, enabling persistent access to compromised Microsoft 365 environments.
